providers.name: OpenAI

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer <API key or workload-identity access token>. Optional OpenAI-Organization and OpenAI-Project headers (API overview page).

models.notes: gpt-5-nano ($0.05 in / $0.40 out per 1M) is the cheapest text model with a model page; it is a reasoning-token model (page: 'Reasoning token support'), Chat Completions and Responses supported. gpt-4.1-nano ($0.10/$0.40) is the cheapest non-reasoning option. gpt-6-luna ($0.10/$0.50, 'most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks', 1.05M context) is the current-generation cost tier: reasoning.effort supports none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max; Chat Completions function calling only with reasoning_effort=none. gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra are the higher tiers on the featured list. All ids confirmed on developers.openai.com/api/docs/models and the per-model .md pages 2026-10-20. Earlier reference-doc facts (round 1, chat.md / responses create.md): max_completion_tokens bounds visible + reasoning tokens; max_tokens deprecated and not compatible with o-series; developer role messages replace system with o1 and newer; reasoning_effort values none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max ('Not all reasoning models support every value'); stream_options.include_usage adds a final usage chunk with empty choices, other chunks carry usage null; usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens documented; Responses store defaults true; temperature 0..2; stop up to 4 sequences; seed best-effort; logprobs/top_logprobs 0..20.

deviations.text: gpt-6-luna model page: Chat Completions supports function calling only with reasoning_effort set to none; use the Responses API for built-in tools and function calling

providers.notes: Reference. Base URL now confirmed on the API overview page (curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models example). Rate-limit headers documented on the rate-limits and overview pages: x-ratelimit-limit/remaining/reset-requests and -tokens (plus project-token variants), Retry-After on temporary 429/503; also openai-organization, openai-processing-ms, openai-version, x-request-id. Error codes page documents error type/code pairs (e.g. rate_limit_error, service_unavailable_error). Chat Completions create page 404s at .../methods/create.md; parameters live in resources/chat.md. Chat Completions overview says new projects should try Responses. Round 1 wrongly said gpt-5-nano/gpt-4.1-nano are not listed; they are on the models catalog today.

providers.name: Cerebras Inference

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer <CEREBRAS_API_KEY> (securityScheme BearerAuth in the API reference).

models.notes: Model Catalog lists exactly two Shared Inference models: gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b (llama3.1-8b is no longer listed). gpt-oss-120b is the cheapest ($0.35/$0.75 vs qwen-3.8-27b $0.99/$1.49) and is a reasoning model (reasoning_effort low/medium/high, default medium, reasoning cannot be disabled). qwen-3.8-27b is the alternative reasoning model (supports reasoning_effort none) and the only vision model. Free tier for gpt-oss-120b: 30 req/min, 60k input tokens/min, 1M tokens/day; context 65k free / 131k paid; max output 32k free / 40k paid.

deviations.text: OpenAI compatibility page: only n: 1 is supported (API reference schema enum [1]).
Tool streaming: use standard streaming with stream: true; do not send tool_stream.

Images: standard image_url content parts, but the url must be a base64 PNG or JPEG data URI; external HTTPS image URLs and image_url.detail are not supported (400 'HTTPS image URLs are not supported'); images only on user messages and only on vision-capable models (qwen-3.8-27b); gpt-oss-120b has no image input.

service_tier is not available with Shared Inference (private preview, dedicated endpoints only); prediction is limited by endpoint and model availability and is not available for qwen-3.8-27b on shared endpoints.
Combining tools with response_format is model-dependent; gpt-oss-120b rejects requests containing both fields.
developer role is supported only by gpt-oss-120b; system and developer both map to a developer-level instruction layer, so the same prompt may behave differently than on OpenAI.
max_tokens is an alias of max_completion_tokens (do not send both); reasoning tokens count toward max_completion_tokens and completion usage.
stop accepts up to four sequences.

temperature range 0-2; logprobs (boolean), top_logprobs 0-20, seed (best effort, determinism not guaranteed), frequency_penalty/presence_penalty -2..2 and logit_bias are documented request parameters.

response_format json_schema with strict:true uses constrained decoding but requires additionalProperties:false on every object and rejects recursive schemas, oneOf/allOf/not, nullable:true, if/then/else, patternProperties, root unions; json_object is not compatible with streaming (stream must be false).

gpt-oss-120b reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, high only (default medium; none not supported); Cerebras-specific reasoning_format (parsed/raw/hidden/none) and clear_thinking must be passed via extra_body in OpenAI clients; with parsed format reasoning is returned in message.reasoning / delta.reasoning.
Assistant messages may carry a 'reasoning' field supplied back in history; supported behavior varies by model.
Usage reports prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (prompt caching is automatic).

Error codes listed: 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 413, 422 (UnprocessableEntityError), 429, 500, 503. Round-1 claim that validation errors return 400 instead of 422 is not supported by the docs. Error body shape and rate-limit headers are not documented in the fetched pages.
The Chat Completions request schema does not list stream_options (include_usage), so streaming usage behavior is undocumented.

providers.notes: Compatibility table, request-parameter schema and prices read from the official pages (pricing page itself returned 403 through the proxy; prices taken from the model pages $0.35/$0.75 gpt-oss-120b, $0.99/$1.49 qwen-3.8-27b). Round 1's qwen-3.8-27b reference and gpt-oss-120b pricing were right; its 'only gpt-oss-120b in catalog' and '400 instead of 422' claims were wrong. No Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoint appears in the docs index. Free tier exists (rate limits per model page); CI-friendly with a free key. inference-docs.cerebras.ai fails WebFetch DNS but works via curl.

providers.name: Alibaba DashScope (Model Studio, Qwen)

auth.notes: Model Studio API key as Bearer token. Keys are bound to the region they were created in; a key from another region returns HTTP 401 'Incorrect API key provided' (code invalid_api_key). Docs now recommend workspace-specific domains (Singapore: https://{WorkspaceId}.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1; Virginia: {WorkspaceId}.us-east-1; Beijing: {WorkspaceId}.cn-beijing; Hong Kong: {WorkspaceId}.cn-hongkong; Tokyo: {WorkspaceId}.ap-northeast-1; Frankfurt: {WorkspaceId}.eu-central-1 on the Responses page). base_url above is the legacy Singapore host the docs say to migrate from; the Responses and Anthropic pages state 'The existing domain remains fully functional'. Legacy Beijing host: https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1. The chat page itself only lists the workspace domains, so prefer the workspace URL if a WorkspaceId is available.

models.notes: qwen3.7-flash is the cheapest current model on the Singapore pricing page (Qwen-Flash table, tiered: <=32K input tokens $0.03 in / $0.13 out). qwen3.8-flash ($0.15 / $0.47, <=1M tokens) is listed on the Recommended-models page and takes reasoning_effort low/medium/xhigh (default xhigh) or enable_thinking. qwen-flash ($0.05/$0.40 <=256K) and qwen3.5-flash ($0.1/$0.4) also exist. Both chosen ids appear in the Responses-API and Anthropic-endpoint supported-model lists. Whether qwen3.7-flash thinks by default was not determined (default table is behind a 'Supported models' link not read). Rate limits Singapore: qwen3.7-flash 15,000 RPM / 5,000,000 TPM; qwen3.8-flash 'Dynamic Rate Limiting'.

price_usd_per_mtok.source: official-page: Singapore (International deployment) qwen3.7-flash, input tokens per request 0<Token<=32K; higher tiers 32K-256K $0.10/$0.40, 256K-1M $0.20/$0.80. Free quota in Singapore only (1M tokens, valid 90 days from activation).

anthropic_messages_endpoint.url: https://{WorkspaceId}.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic (SDK base_url; POST .../apps/anthropic/v1/messages). Auth via x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer. Supported list includes qwen3.7-flash, qwen3.8-flash, qwen-flash.

deviations.text: temperature valid range is [0, 2) (2 itself excluded); a value of 0 is not recommended; do not set both temperature and top_p
top_p valid range is (0, 1.0]; top_k, repetition_penalty are non-standard and go in extra_body (Python SDK)
n valid values 1-4; chat API reference says only supported by Qwen3 (non-thinking mode) models, compat page says only qwen-plus; n is fixed at 1 when tools is set; n=0 equals n=1
seed supported (range [0, 2^31-1] on the chat reference; compat page says unsigned 64-bit); reproducibility is best-effort
stop accepts a string or an array; array elements cannot mix token_ids and strings; no maximum count documented
logprobs/top_logprobs supported only for qwen-plus snapshot models (not stable alias), qwen3-vl-plus series and Qwen3 open-source models; top_logprobs range [0, 5]; reasoning_content gets no logprobs
Only messages[0] may have the system role; valid roles listed are system, user, assistant (and tool for results); no developer role
Compat page: 'In general, user and assistant roles alternate, and the last element must have the user role'
Message name field is not listed in the message schemas (system/user/assistant/tool objects have content and role only; tool has tool_call_id)
User content may be a string or an array of parts (text, image_url, input_audio, video, video_url); system and assistant content are documented as strings
image_url parts take a URL or Base64 data URL, but only multimodal models (Qwen-VL/Omni, newer Qwen3.x multimodal) accept them; min_pixels/max_pixels/vl_high_resolution_images are non-standard
max_tokens is 'to be deprecated'; meaning varies by model (glm-5.3 and deepseek-v4 count answer plus chain-of-thought, 'other models' count the answer only)

max_completion_tokens supported for Qwen Flash 3.5 and later (and Max 3.7+, Plus 3.5+, Kimi k2.5+, GLM 5+, MiniMax M2.5+, DeepSeek v4-pro+); limits chain-of-thought plus answer; may overshoot by up to 10 tokens
tool_choice: Qwen series do not support 'required'; thinking-mode models do not support forcing a specific function (named tool_choice); default auto; parallel_tool_calls defaults to false
Compat page: the tools parameter cannot be used with stream=True at the same time (while the chat reference documents a non-standard tool_stream flag for Qwen3.5+/GLM series; docs conflict)

response_format supports text, json_object, json_schema (with strict); json_object and json_schema are supported by different models; json_object requires the word JSON in the prompt or the call errors
stream_options.include_usage defaults to false and only takes effect when stream is true; usage arrives in the final chunk (choices empty)
usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is returned (implicit and explicit caching; explicit caching uses cache_control: {type: ephemeral} on user content parts)
Thinking toggled by non-standard enable_thinking (extra_body in Python SDK, top-level over raw HTTP) plus thinking_budget; thinking text returned in reasoning_content

reasoning_effort is standard but valid values/defaults vary per model: qwen3.8 family xhigh (default)/medium/low with max,high->xhigh, minimal->low, none->enable_thinking=false; glm-5.3 and kimi-k3 low/high/max; DeepSeek-V4 high/max; other values error; cannot be combined with thinking_budget on qwen3.8
preserve_thinking (default true on qwen3.8-max/flash) requires historical reasoning_content to be sent back in assistant messages, not concatenated into content; billed as input
presence_penalty supported only on Qwen commercial models and open-source qwen1.5 and later; system_fingerprint is returned as an empty string

Responses API (/compatible-mode/v1/responses) is supported for listed models incl. qwen3.7-flash and qwen3.8-flash; previous_response_id keeps context, response ids valid 7 days; models outside the list get only basic compatibility; a legacy path /api/v2/apps/protocols/compatible-mode/v1/responses is unmaintained

Errors: wrong-region key gives HTTP 401 with code invalid_api_key and message 'Incorrect API key provided'; RPM/TPM breaches return 429; exhausted free quota returns 403; rate-limit response headers are not documented

providers.notes: Read via curl through the sandbox proxy (WebFetch itself fails DNS for every host; curl reaches www.alibabacloud.com, not help.aliyun.com/dashscope.aliyuncs.com APIs). Pages show 'Last Updated' Oct 11-19, 2026. Intl and China regions are separate accounts/keys. Free quota is Singapore only (90 days). Not read: deep-thinking page, error-code page, GET /models. The compat page and the chat API reference disagree on n (qwen-plus vs Qwen3 non-thinking) and seed range; the chat API reference is the newer-looking page.

providers.name: Databricks Foundation Model APIs

auth.notes: Databricks personal access token (dapi...) or OAuth token as Bearer; docs examples use curl -u token:$DATABRICKS_TOKEN and api_key=<token> in the OpenAI client. Base URL is workspace-specific. Docs show two chat surfaces: Unity Gateway model services at <workspace>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1 (model = system.ai.<name>, e.g. system.ai.meta-llama-3-1-8b-instruct) and legacy serving endpoints at <workspace>/serving-endpoints (model = endpoint name, e.g. databricks-meta-llama-3-1-8b-instruct).

models.notes: Supported Models page lists 'Model service name: system.ai.meta-llama-3-1-8b-instruct / Endpoint name: databricks-meta-llama-3-1-8b-instruct' and 'system.ai.gpt-oss-20b / databricks-gpt-oss-20b' (GPT OSS 20B is a lightweight reasoning-only model, reasoning_effort low/medium/high, default medium, 'none' treated as unset). Both are also in the Query-foundation-models list. Pricing is DBU-based and not published on these pages, so 'cheapest' is unverified; Llama 3.1 8B is the smallest chat model listed (max output 8,192 tokens). Use endpoint names (databricks-*) when calling the serving-endpoints base URL.

deviations.text: Two chat base URL patterns are documented: <workspace>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1 (Unity Gateway model services, system.ai.* names) and <workspace>/serving-endpoints (endpoint names databricks-*); the Responses path is /ai-gateway/openai/v1/responses (also /serving-endpoints/responses). Foundation model requests are routed through Unity Gateway.

Chat request fields documented: messages, max_tokens, stream, temperature, top_p, top_k, stop, n, tool_choice, tools, response_format, logprobs, top_logprobs, reasoning_effort, service_tier; max_completion_tokens is not listed.
stream defaults to true in the Chat request table.

Message roles are system, user, assistant, tool (no developer role); list-of-parts content is documented for external Claude models only, use string content for other providers/open models; image content must be base64 data (URLs not supported).
The n parameter is only available for provisioned throughput endpoints.

Function is the only supported tool type, max 32 functions; parallel function calling is not supported (public preview limitation); tool JSON schema subset: no pattern, anyOf/oneOf/allOf/prefixItems/$ref, type lists except [type,'null'], max 16 keys; function description is required.

Structured outputs are OpenAI-compatible for Foundation Model APIs (json_schema with strict; schema subset, max 64 keys). For Claude models only json_schema is supported (json_object not supported), structured outputs are not supported with streaming, and response_format cannot be combined with tools/tool_choice.

reasoning_effort is only accepted by a limited set of models; accepted values (none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max) and defaults vary by model; GPT OSS accepts low/medium/high ('minimal'->low, 'xhigh'/'max'->high, 'none' treated as unset); GLM 5.3 Flash and GLM 5.3 reject 'none'.
Reasoning output shape varies by model family (Claude via Anthropic Messages thinking/output_config.effort; reasoning content returned as content items with summary) and differs from OpenAI fields.

Pay-per-token Responses API: background, store and previous_response_id are not supported and return a 400 error; 'conversation' is also unsupported on the Open Responses surface; the native OpenAI Responses passthrough is for OpenAI models and external models support all parameters; code interpreter and web search tools are not supported.
Prompt caching cache_control is accepted only by Databricks-hosted Claude models.

Rate limits for pay-per-token endpoints are ITPM, OTPM and queries-per-hour per model; max_tokens is used to reserve output-token capacity and a request that would exceed OTPM is rejected immediately with 429; workspace QPS 200; request payload 4 MB; model execution limit 597 seconds per request (30 minutes for streaming to open models, not the legacy Llama 3.1 models).
Max output tokens per response: Llama 3.1 8B / 3.3 70B / Gemma 3 12B / Llama 4 Maverick 8,192; GPT OSS 20B/120B 25,000; DeepSeek V4 384,000.

Response/stream note: output returned in choices; usage returned in every chunk when streaming (Anthropic-format differences documented for Claude); finish_reason maps end_turn/stop_sequence/max_tokens/tool_use to stop/stop/length/tool_calls.

providers.notes: Read from docs.databricks.com (AWS) via curl and the Azure Databricks mirror on learn.microsoft.com via WebFetch (docs.databricks.com fails WebFetch DNS). Requires a Databricks workspace; the base URL is a pattern, so record the host in a DATABRICKS_BASE_URL-style variable (secret name follows the brief; docs use DATABRICKS_TOKEN). Pay-per-token pricing is DBU-based and was not found, so price is null. Not CI-friendly without a paid workspace. Model catalog churns quickly (docs list GPT-6, Claude Fable/Opus 5.x, Gemini 4 etc.); confirm availability in the target workspace and region.

providers.name: DeepInfra

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer <DEEPINFRA_API_KEY>; the API reference also lists x-api-key / xi-api-key header variants.

models.notes: This id is used throughout the official chat docs and is listed on the Reasoning Models page (also DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, zai-org/GLM-5.2, moonshotai/Kimi-K3, inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash). It is a hybrid reasoning model: reasoning_effort 'none' (or reasoning.enabled=false) turns reasoning off, so the same id serves as chat and reasoning model. Whether it is the cheapest chat model could not be verified: the model catalog/pricing pages (deepinfra.com) are unreachable; round 1's meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is not mentioned in the current docs.

deviations.text: Docs state the API may not be 100% compatible with all OpenAI parameters.

Supported parameters table: model, messages (roles system, user, assistant), max_tokens, stream, temperature (0-2), top_p, stop, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, response_format, tools/tool_choice, service_tier (priority/flex), fail_fast, reasoning_effort. The API reference additionally lists seed, logprobs, stream_options, top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty, reasoning, prompt_cache_key, chat_template_kwargs and others; max_completion_tokens is not listed.
max_tokens: hard cap 16384 tokens for most models; unset max_tokens defaults to model context minus input or 65536, whichever is smaller; response continuation by trailing assistant message.
Messages schema: (user, assistant, tool)* plus one system message anywhere; no developer role in the schema; optional name on user/assistant/system messages.
n: 1-4 (default 1).
stop: overview table says up to 4 sequences, API reference schema says up to 16 sequences (docs disagree).
temperature 0-2; seed accepted (determinism not guaranteed); logprobs/top_logprobs (1-20) supported across all request modes.
Streaming: usage arrives in the final chunk together with finish_reason (choices not empty); stream_options.include_usage defaults to true (OpenAI default is off); continuous_usage_stats optional.
response_format: text, json_object, json_schema (strict:true recommended) and a non-standard regex type; JSON mode can increase hallucination.

Tool calling: single and parallel calls (quality may vary), tool_choice auto/none (reference also lists required and a named function), streaming supported, nested calls not supported; docs advise avoiding system messages when using tool calling.
Images: image_url accepts a public URL or a base64 data URI on vision models.

reasoning_effort (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max per reference; overview/reasoning page list none/low/medium/high) is a top-level parameter (docs show extra_body in the Python SDK); a `reasoning` object {effort, enabled} is also supported; non-reasoning models silently ignore both; reasoning tokens bill as output.
Assistant messages accept reasoning_content (string) for replay.
Prompt caching is automatic; usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens reports cached tokens; prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_options (ttl 5m/1h) optional.

Rate limit: 200 concurrent requests per model (not per-minute); 429 'Rate limited'; fail_fast returns 429 with OpenAI-style error {message,type:invalid_request_error,param,code:engine_overloaded}; no rate-limit headers documented.
service_tier priority (+50%) / flex (-20%) on tagged models; an unsupported tier is served at standard tier with no error.

providers.notes: docs.deepinfra.com .md pages and the OpenAPI chat-completions reference were read via curl (WebFetch DNS fails). deepinfra.com and api.deepinfra.com are blocked by the proxy, so price ($0.09 in / $0.18 out for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) is search-summary from DeepInfra's model page as quoted by a web search; Responses endpoint and GET /models are not documented in the fetched pages (round 1's models_list=true removed). Anthropic Messages endpoint documented at https://api.deepinfra.com/anthropic (POST /anthropic/v1/messages, also count_tokens). Also an HF router provider.

providers.name: DeepSeek

auth.notes: Examples send 'Authorization: Bearer ${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}'; chat endpoint is {base_url}/chat/completions (no /v1 needed).

models.notes: Models & Pricing lists only deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) and deepseek-v4-pro (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813). Thinking mode is ON by default for both: send thinking:{type:'disabled'} (or reasoning_effort none) for plain chat and thinking enabled with reasoning_effort low/high/max for reasoning. Legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are accepted but retired (served by flash). deepseek-chat / deepseek-reasoner are not mentioned on the pages read.

deviations.text: The chat request schema lists model enum [deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro]; legacy deepseek-v4-flash names are still accepted but served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and billed at Flash price.
stop accepts up to 16 sequences.
temperature (<=2) has no effect in thinking mode, which is the default; presence_penalty and frequency_penalty are deprecated and have no effect without raising an error.

top_p only takes effect in thinking mode on deepseek-flash (effective range 0.95-1.0, lower values clamped to 0.95); on deepseek-v4-pro it is ignored in thinking mode (fixed 0.95 with tools, otherwise 1.0).
tool_choice required and named-function choices are not supported in thinking mode and return a 400; disable thinking first.

response_format accepts only text or json_object (no json_schema); JSON mode requires the prompt itself to ask for JSON or the model may emit unending whitespace. Tool-call strict mode is a Beta feature.
max_tokens range is 1 to 384K; default 8K in non-thinking mode, 64K in thinking mode (128K with reasoning_effort max). max_completion_tokens is not in the documented request schema.
n and seed are not listed in the documented chat completion request schema.
logprobs (boolean) and top_logprobs (<=20) are listed in the request schema.
Thinking is toggled with a non-standard thinking:{type: enabled|disabled} body field (default enabled; pass via extra_body in the OpenAI SDK) and reasoning_effort accepts none, low, high, max.
reasoning_effort mapping: minimal->low, medium->high, xhigh->high, ultra->max are accepted for compatibility and silently remapped; default effort is high.
Chain of thought is returned in message.reasoning_content at the same level as content (thinking mode only).
If the request carries tools, reasoning_content of all previous turns must be passed back; without tools it is ignored and not added to the context.

stream_options requires stream:true (else 400). The final content chunk always carries usage even when include_usage is omitted; no separate usage-only chunk is emitted and that last chunk has exactly one choice with no new content.
usage includes prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens plus DeepSeek's prompt_cache_hit_tokens and prompt_cache_miss_tokens.

User messages accept content parts text, image_url (jpeg/png/gif/webp, http(s) or data URL, detail low/high/original/auto) and file; images are supported on deepseek-flash only (deepseek-v4-pro: vision not supported).
message name is documented as an optional participant name on system, user, assistant messages.
Chat message roles in the schema are system, user, assistant, tool; developer is not listed.

Error codes: 400 invalid format, 401, 402 insufficient balance, 422 invalid parameters, 429 rate limit/concurrency, 500, 503; concurrency limit per account is 2500 (flash) / 500 (v4-pro) and exceeding it returns 429; no rate-limit headers are documented.
Responses API (base_url https://api.deepseek.com) is supported for deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro with function tools and streaming semantic events (no [DONE]).
Responses API: previous_response_id is not supported (stateless API).
Responses API: conversation is not supported (stateless API).
Responses API: store is not supported; the response always carries store: false.
Responses API: background is not supported.
Responses API: metadata is not supported.
Responses API: include is not supported.
Responses API: prompt (reusable prompts) is not supported.
Responses API: truncation is not supported; requests exceeding the context window return a 400.
Responses API: service_tier is not supported.
Responses API: safety_identifier is not supported.
Responses API: prompt_cache_key / prompt_cache_retention are not supported (context caching is automatic).
Responses API: context_management is not supported.
Responses API: stream_options is not supported.
Responses API: parallel_tool_calls is ignored (parallel tool calling is always enabled).
Responses API: max_tool_calls is ignored.
Responses API: reasoning.summary is accepted but no summary is generated.
Responses API: text.verbosity is accepted but has no effect.

Responses API: tools other than function (and web_search on deepseek-v4-pro, and the apply_patch custom tool) are ignored: file_search, code_interpreter, computer_use, mcp; web_search is ignored with deepseek-flash.
Responses API: developer role messages are treated as user; File inputs are not supported; reasoning input items drop summary and encrypted_content.
Anthropic endpoint: anthropic-version header is ignored; anthropic-beta is ignored for /messages (except files-api-2025-04-14 for file image sources).
Anthropic endpoint: container, mcp_servers and service_tier are ignored; metadata supports only user_id.
Anthropic endpoint: thinking is supported but budget_tokens is ignored; output_config supports only effort; top_k is ignored.
Anthropic endpoint: cache_control (tools, text, tool_use, tool_result), citations and tool_result is_error are ignored; disable_parallel_tool_use is ignored for tool_choice auto/any/tool.
Anthropic endpoint: document, search_result, redacted_thinking, code_execution_tool_result, mcp_tool_use, mcp_tool_result and container_upload content blocks are not supported.
Anthropic endpoint: Model names starting with claude are accepted: claude-opus* maps to deepseek-v4-pro and other claude* to deepseek-flash; other unsupported names return 400.

providers.notes: Read via curl through the agent proxy (WebFetch DNS fails). Price confirmed from pricing table: deepseek-flash peak (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri, excluding Chinese holidays) $0.30 in (cache miss) / $1.20 out, cache hit $0.006; off-peak half ($0.15 / $0.60 / $0.003). deepseek-v4-pro peak $1.32/$3.96. Round-1 'responses' and 'models_list' inferences are now confirmed by the Responses API and List Models pages. Round-1 legacy-name retirement conflict resolved: pages now only mention deepseek-v4-flash legacy names. Items marked 'not listed in the request schema' (n, seed, max_completion_tokens, developer role) are absences in the API reference, not explicit statements; verify with probes.

providers.name: Fireworks AI

auth.notes: 'Authenticate with your Fireworks API key as a bearer token' (Responses page); the OpenAI client takes the key as api_key.

models.notes: Ids use accounts/fireworks/models/<slug>; slugs are taken from the model links in the Serverless Pricing table (app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/<slug>), which lists NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B at $0.05/$0.20 (cheapest named row) and OpenAI GPT OSS 120B at $0.15/$0.60. Whether Nemotron Lightning supports tools/reasoning was not checked. Other rows: GLM 5.3 Flash $0.15/$0.50, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30/$1.20. gpt-oss-120b is a Harmony model (effort low/medium/high only). Unlisted models are priced by size ($0.10 under 4B, $0.20 for 4B-16B, $0.90 above 16B).

deviations.text: max_tokens is lowered to fit the context window instead of erroring when prompt plus max_tokens exceeds it; context_length_exceeded_behavior=error restores OpenAI-style errors (default truncate).
max_completion_tokens is an alias of max_tokens and cannot be specified together with max_tokens.
stop accepts up to 4 sequences.
Streaming usage is included by default in a final chunk (the one with finish_reason set) rather than only when stream_options.include_usage is set; include_usage=false opts out.
tool_choice accepts auto, none, any and required (any is an alias of required) or a named function; allowed_tools is also accepted.
Reasoning is returned in message.reasoning_content (and delta.reasoning_content when streaming), separate from content.

reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, max, none, adaptive (MiniMax M3 only), booleans and integer token budgets (Fireworks extensions); Harmony models (GPT-OSS 120B/20B) accept only low, medium, high (default medium) and error on none/false/integers.
On DeepSeek V4 models reasoning_effort 'medium' is silently promoted to 'high' and 'xhigh' to 'max'.
reasoning_effort 'auto' is dropped so the model default applies (NIM compatibility page).
thinking and reasoning_effort cannot both be sent in the same request (validation error).
Using response_format json_schema disables reasoning output; to get both, put the schema in the prompt and omit response_format.
Models that cannot disable reasoning return 400 for reasoning_effort 'none' (and for enable_thinking:false mapped to none).
Error bodies for inference use {"error": {"code": "NOT_FOUND", ...}, "request_id": ...}; codes documented: 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 408, 412, 413, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 520.

Rate-limit response headers are X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Prompt, X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Cache-Adjusted-Prompt and X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Generated (limits only, tokens per minute); no remaining/reset headers are documented. Cached tokens are reported in the fireworks-cached-prompt-tokens header.

NIM/vLLM request extras with no Chat Completions equivalent are stripped so requests are not rejected and do not change generation: guided_regex, guided_decoding_backend, stop_token_ids, include_stop_str_in_output, skip_special_tokens, spaces_between_special_tokens, best_of, use_beam_search, add_generation_prompt, continue_final_message, add_special_tokens, detokenize, allowed_token_ids, bad_words, include_reasoning, nvext.

chat_template_kwargs keys other than thinking toggles (e.g. parallel_reasoning_mode) are dropped; enable_thinking:false maps to reasoning_effort none; truncate_prompt_tokens is renamed prompt_truncate_len.
Responses API is served at /inference/v1/responses; responses are stored by default and previous_response_id continues a conversation; store=false opts out.
Responses API does not support code_interpreter, file_search or image_generation tools.
Responses API does not support refusal content parts.
Responses API does not support GET /v1/responses/{id}/input_items.
Responses API does not support background and stream together.
Responses API supports only include value message.output_text.logprobs; other values are not supported.
defer_loading has no effect on the Responses API (deferred tools are exposed eagerly).
Anthropic Messages endpoint: model must be a Fireworks model identifier, not an Anthropic model name.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: The anthropic-version header is not required and is ignored.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: max_tokens is required and must be > 0 (omitting it returns 400 invalid_request_error).
Anthropic Messages endpoint: inference_geo is deprecated in favor of data residency and should be removed from requests.

Anthropic Messages endpoint: thinking.budget_tokens is converted to a reasoning_effort band (>=10000 high, 5000-9999 medium, 1024-4999 low); output_config.effort wins when both are present; thinking.type disabled sends reasoning_effort none.

Anthropic Messages endpoint: Enforced 400s: thinking.budget_tokens required (>=1024) when thinking is enabled, max_tokens must exceed budget_tokens, enabled thinking cannot combine with forced tool_choice any/tool, and assistant turns cannot be pre-filled while thinking is enabled or adaptive.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: document content blocks and image blocks with source.type 'file' are rejected.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: Only POST /v1/messages is served; /v1/messages/count_tokens returns 404 and /v1/messages/batches is unavailable.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: Anthropic server tools (code execution, memory, web fetch, web search) are not supported; declaring web_search_20250305 returns 400.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: Server-tool metadata fields (caller, container) and server_tool_use usage tracking are not supported.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: Tool schema fields eager_input_streaming, cache_control, allowed_callers and input_examples are not supported.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: output_config.speed is not supported yet.

Anthropic Messages endpoint: Error bodies use the Anthropic envelope; status codes follow Anthropic conventions (422 reported as 400, billing 402, oversized 413); unknown model or unrouted path returns the standard Fireworks error body instead.
Anthropic Messages endpoint: input_tokens excludes cache-read tokens (reported as cache_read_input_tokens) and cache_creation_input_tokens is always 0.

providers.name: Groq

auth.notes: Examples send 'Authorization: Bearer $GROQ_API_KEY'; the OpenAI client takes the Groq key as api_key.

models.notes: gpt-oss-20b is the cheapest production model with a public price on the models page ($0.075/$0.30). llama-3.1-8b-instant shows 'Contact Sales' (Enterprise) there and the deprecations page lists it for shutdown on 08/16/26 with openai/gpt-oss-20b as replacement. gpt-oss-20b is on the reasoning supported-models list; reasoning_effort low/medium/high; reasoning returned in message.reasoning by default. Other reasoning models: openai/gpt-oss-120b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b.

deviations.text: logprobs is listed as unsupported and returns a 400 error if supplied; the API reference says it is not yet supported by any model.
top_logprobs is listed as unsupported and returns a 400 error if supplied; the API reference says it is not yet supported by any model.
logit_bias is listed as unsupported and returns a 400 error if supplied.
messages[].name is listed as unsupported and returns a 400 error if supplied.
n must be 1: the API reference gives range 1-1 and says other values return a 400 response.
frequency_penalty and presence_penalty are documented as not yet supported by any model (API reference); the docs do not say whether a request is rejected.
store and metadata are documented as not currently supported on chat completions.
A temperature of 0 is converted to 1e-8; the docs suggest a float32 > 0 and <= 2 if issues arise.
seed is best effort: determinism is not guaranteed and system_fingerprint should be monitored for backend changes.
stop accepts up to 4 sequences.
max_completion_tokens is the documented output cap parameter (also used in reasoning-page examples).
max_tokens is still accepted but marked Deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens.
stream_options.include_usage adds an extra final chunk before [DONE] with an empty choices array and the usage totals; other chunks carry usage null when it is set.
tool_choice accepts none, auto, required or a named function; at most 128 functions per request.
For gpt-oss models reasoning_format is not supported; reasoning is returned by default in a message.reasoning field and include_reasoning=false suppresses it.
reasoning_effort on gpt-oss-20b/120b accepts low, medium or high (default medium); values outside a model's supported set are rejected with a 400.
include_reasoning is mutually exclusive with reasoning_format.

For non-gpt-oss reasoning models, reasoning_format raw combined with JSON mode or tool use returns a 400; reasoning_format must be parsed or hidden in those modes (it defaults to raw or parsed per the docs).

response_format json_schema with strict:true (constrained decoding) is available only on select models, including openai/gpt-oss-20b and openai/gpt-oss-120b; strict mode requires all fields required and additionalProperties false.

Prompt caching is automatic and only supported on openai/gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-safeguard-20b; cached input tokens get a 50% discount, hits are best effort, and usage reports cached_tokens.

Rate-limit headers: x-ratelimit-limit-requests and -remaining-requests/-reset-requests always refer to requests per DAY, while the -tokens headers refer to tokens per minute; reset values are durations such as 2m59.56s; retry-after (seconds) is only set on a 429.
Text Completions is listed under 'Currently Unsupported OpenAI Features' on the compatibility page.
Audio transcription and translation do not support the vtt and srt response formats.
Responses API is in beta and does not support stateful conversations yet; history must be resent in input.
Responses API is documented as fully compatible for text and image input with function calling.
Responses API does not support previous_response_id.
Responses API does not support store.
Responses API does not support truncation.
Responses API does not support include.
Responses API does not support safety_identifier.
Responses API does not support prompt_cache_key.
Responses API does not support prompt (reusable prompts).

providers.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers

auth.notes: Bearer HF user access token (hf_...), fine-grained with 'Make calls to Inference Providers' permission. Docs examples use env var HF_TOKEN. Optional X-HF-Bill-To header bills a Team/Enterprise org.

models.notes: Both ids appear in the live GET https://router.huggingface.co/v1/models list (checked 2026-10-20: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct served by novita/nscale/featherless-ai/deepinfra, cheapest $0.02/$0.05 via novita and deepinfra; gpt-oss-120b served by 11 providers from $0.037/$0.17 deepinfra up to $0.35/$0.75 cerebras). Provider choice is by suffix :fastest (default), :cheapest, :preferred or a provider name e.g. openai/gpt-oss-120b:groq. Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 (nscale $0.01/$0.03) is a small reasoning model. Llama-3.1-8B providers report supports_tools false.

deviations.text: The router proxies many providers; the exact HTTP request may vary between providers as each has its own API requirements and response formats. Provider is chosen dynamically (:fastest default) with automatic failover when the primary provider is flagged unavailable.

Chat completion API specification documents max_tokens only (no max_completion_tokens, no n parameter); stop is up to 4 sequences; top_logprobs 0-5; tool_choice auto/none/required/function; non-standard tool_prompt.
reasoning_effort is optional; common values none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh; support and defaults are provider and model dependent.
response_format accepts text, json_object and json_schema (name, description, schema, strict).
stream_options.include_usage: extra chunk before [DONE] with usage and an empty choices array; other chunks carry usage null.
Message content parts documented are text and image_url only; messages carry an optional name; the schema lists no developer role and no reasoning field on messages.
temperature 0-2, logprobs, seed are documented request parameters.

Responses API (beta) at https://router.huggingface.co/v1/responses (OpenAI SDK client.responses.create, model ids with optional :provider suffix, reasoning={'effort': low|medium|high}); the guide states all Inference Providers chat completion models should be compatible; store/previous_response_id behavior is not documented in the guide.

Chat Completion only on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no embeddings, images, speech); GET /v1/models returns models across providers with per-provider pricing, context length, supports_tools, supports_structured_output, latency and throughput.

providers.notes: Docs call it a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI chat completions API. Pricing: pay-as-you-go passthrough with no HF markup; free users have no included credits (credit purchase required), PRO $2/month, Team/Enterprise $2 per seat. Anthropic-compatible: Claude Code integration sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://router.huggingface.co with the HF token (SDK appends /v1/messages); request schema not read. Price shown is the cheapest live provider for the chat model, not a fixed price. Because provider selection is dynamic, pin a provider suffix (e.g. :deepinfra, :novita) for repeatable CI probes. Secret name follows the brief's rule (HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY); docs use HF_TOKEN. No error-shape or rate-limit-header facts in the fetched pages.

providers.name: Mistral La Plateforme

auth.notes: curl examples and the error glossary specify 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'.

models.notes: Model cards: Ministral 3 3B (api names ministral-3b-2512, alias ministral-3b-latest) $0.1/$0.1 per M tokens, 256k context, function calling and structured outputs; Mistral Small 4 (mistral-small-2603, alias mistral-small-latest) $0.15/$0.6, 256k context, adjustable reasoning via reasoning_effort. The reasoning page lists reasoning_effort support for mistral-small-latest, mistral-medium-3-5, mistral-large-4-0 and zai-glm-5-3 (low/high/max, no none). Magistral models are deprecated.

deviations.text: The Migration guide says the Mistral Chat Completions API follows the same request structure as OpenAI and documents pointing an OpenAI client at https://api.mistral.ai/v1 with only base URL and model name changed.
The seed parameter is named random_seed (integer or null) in the documented request schema.
max_tokens is the documented output cap; max_completion_tokens is not in the documented request schema.
Documented message roles are system, user, assistant and tool; developer is not listed.

tool_choice accepts auto, none, any and required (any/required force a tool call without guaranteeing which tool) or a named function; at most 128 tools per request; parallel_tool_calls defaults true.
n and logprobs/top_logprobs are in the request schema (n: input tokens billed once).

Temperature is recommended between 0.0 and 0.7 with a model-dependent default; the error glossary gives 'temperature outside 0 to 1 range' as an example of an unsupported parameter value returning 400.

With reasoning_effort high, message.content is a list of chunks (a thinking chunk with a thinking list of text chunks, plus text chunks) instead of a plain string; with none it is a plain string. zai-glm-5-3 always returns a chunk list.
Multi-turn reasoning requires replaying the full assistant message including the thinking chunk; stripping it degrades quality.

reasoning_effort enum is none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh in the schema, but support is per model (mistral-small-latest, mistral-medium-3-5, mistral-large-4-0; zai-glm-5-3 takes low/high/max and not none).
response_format supports text, json_object and json_schema (schema-following JSON mode); JSON mode needs the word JSON in the prompt and does not guarantee a specific schema.
stream_options.include_usage must be explicitly set to receive token usage in stream events (Known limitations); the chat request schema in the API reference does not list stream_options.
prompt_cache_key is supported and cached tokens are billed at 10% of the input price; the usage field names for cached tokens are not documented on the pages read.
Error glossary uses 400 for malformed requests and 422 for validation errors (wrong type, enum value not allowed); 402 for billing blocks; 429 on rate limits.
Only the X-RateLimit-Remaining response header is named in the docs; limits are per organization, requests per second and tokens per minute enforced independently.
Mistral-specific extras in the request schema: prompt_mode, safe_prompt, random_seed, min_tokens, top_k, repetition_penalty, prediction, guardrails, service_tier (auto, standard_only).
Images: max 20 MB each; PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP; vision availability depends on the model.

providers.notes: Read via curl through the agent proxy (WebFetch DNS fails); prices come from the docs model cards because mistral.ai/pricing was not fetched. Mistral is an own-API provider that documents OpenAI-client use via base URL only, not a parameter-level compatibility page. responses is null: no Responses endpoint appears in the API reference navigation (Mistral has Beta Conversations instead). models_list true from the 'List Available Models API' reference and the Models section. Absences marked in deviations (max_completion_tokens, developer role) are not in the request schema, not explicit statements. Round-1 'Mistral Small 4 / mistral-small-latest' and reasoning_effort claims confirmed; round-1 cheapest chat model changed to ministral-3b-latest ($0.1/$0.1).

providers.name: Moonshot AI (Kimi)

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY. Keys from platform.kimi.ai are independent from keys of other regional Kimi platforms; mixing returns 401. No free tier: minimum recharge $1 to start (cumulative $5 recharge earns a $5 voucher); kimi-k3 is unlocked after a successful top-up (min $1). Rate limits are tiered by cumulative recharge (RPM/TPM/TPD/concurrency, shared across models, enforced per user not per key); the tier table is JS-rendered and was not readable.

models.notes: Current models on the Model List page: kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, kimi-k2.6. kimi-k2.5, moonshot-v1-*, kimi-k2* were discontinued (Aug 31 / May 25 2026). kimi-k2.6 is the cheapest current model ($0.95 in / $4.00 out per 1M); it thinks by default and thinking can be disabled with extra_body {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}. kimi-k3 ($3.00 in / $15.00 out) always reasons, takes top-level reasoning_effort low/high/max (default max). kimi-k2.7-code always thinks and cannot disable it.

price_usd_per_mtok.source: official-page: pricing table for kimi-k2.6, cache-miss input; cached input $0.16. kimi-k3: input $3.00, cached $0.30, cache write 5min $3.00 / 1h $6.00, output $15.00. kimi-k2.7-code: $0.95 in / $4.00 out, cached $0.19.

deviations.text: temperature range is [0, 1] (OpenAI [0, 2]); kimi-k2.6 fixed at 1.0 (thinking) / 0.6 (non-thinking), kimi-k2.7-code and kimi-k3 fixed at 1.0; any other value returns an error; top_p fixed 0.95
n is fixed at 1 for kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code and kimi-k2.6; temperature 0 (or near 0) allows one choice only and temperature 0 with n>1 returns invalid_request_error
presence_penalty and frequency_penalty fixed at 0; passing any other value returns an error; the deprecated functions/function_call parameters are not supported
max_tokens is deprecated in favour of max_completion_tokens (kimi-k3 default 131072, max 1048576); reasoning_content tokens count toward the limit
stop: up to 5 strings, each at most 32 bytes
logprobs (boolean) and top_logprobs (0-20) are listed in the chat request schema
Message roles are system, user, assistant, tool (no developer); optional name field per message; non-standard partial:true on the last assistant message enables Partial Mode
content may be a string or an array of text, image_url, video_url parts; image_url/video_url carry a base64 data URL or an ms://<file_id> reference (remote http URLs are not documented)
tool_choice: kimi-k3 supports auto/none/required/named function; kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.7-code do not support 'required' and return an error
response_format supports text, json_object and json_schema (name + schema, strict); kimi-k2.6 is unstable with complex schemas ($ref may return a code block, oneOf may be ignored)
stream_options.include_usage adds a final chunk with empty choices and usage; in addition Kimi places usage in the final chunk of each choice (choice.usage); intermediate chunks carry usage: null

usage.cached_tokens and usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (plus cache_write_tokens) are returned; automatic prefix caching with prompt_cache_key / prompt_cache_options.ttl (5m or 1h) request fields
Reasoning returned in non-standard reasoning_content (message and delta; always streamed before content); kimi-k2.6 uses extra_body thinking {type: enabled|disabled, keep}; kimi-k3 always thinks
reasoning_effort ('low', 'high', 'max', default max) is only supported by kimi-k3; kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.7-code do not support it
Complete assistant messages including reasoning_content must be passed back unchanged (Preserved Thinking always on for kimi-k3 and kimi-k2.7-code; thinking.keep='all' for kimi-k2.6)

/v1/responses is documented for kimi-k3 only; its request schema has input, instructions, stream, max_output_tokens, reasoning.effort, text.format, tools, tool_choice, include, prompt_cache_* and no store or previous_response_id fields
Responses request schema lists no store/previous_response_id (absence in schema, not an explicit 'unsupported' statement)

Errors use {error: {type, message}} with types such as invalid_request_error, rate_limit_reached_error, engine_overloaded_error; 429 engine_overloaded advises honoring Retry-After; X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset are documented only for the web-search endpoints

providers.name: Perplexity (Orchestrator API)

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer <PERPLEXITY_API_KEY>. The Orchestrator API is in private preview (email api@perplexity.ai for access), so a standard key may not be enough.

models.notes: Both ids are on the Orchestrator Models & Pricing page (creator/model-name slugs; the catalog is also the allowlist, unknown model returns 400). glm-5.3-flash is the cheapest listed ($0.15/$0.50 per Mtok) and the Agent API models page calls GLM 5.3 / 5.3 Flash 'Z.AI reasoning models', so it can double as the cheap reasoning model; kimi-k3 ($3/$15) is the documented flagship reasoning model and accepts minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max effort. Other catalog ids: perplexity/glm-5.3, perplexity/deepseek-v4-pro-0813. Legacy Sonar models (sonar, sonar-reasoning-pro) are not in the current docs; Sonar Chat Completions support ended 2026-09-27.

deviations.text: Orchestrator API accepts the OpenAI Chat Completions schema with a defined subset of parameters; a request using an unsupported parameter fails with HTTP 400 naming the parameter.

Rejected with a 400: seed, logit_bias, top_logprobs, functions, function_call, modalities, audio, prediction, web_search_options, moderation, verbosity, stream_options.include_obfuscation=true, plus any unrecognized top-level field.
Accepted only at their default values: n (1), logprobs (false), store (false), presence_penalty (0), frequency_penalty (0).
Accepted but not forwarded to the model: user, safety_identifier, metadata.

Honored: model, messages, stream, stream_options.include_usage, max_completion_tokens, max_tokens (legacy alias), temperature, top_p, stop (up to 4 sequences), reasoning_effort, service_tier (auto/default/flex/priority), response_format (text/json_schema/json_object), tools, tool_choice (incl. allowed_tools), parallel_tool_calls, prompt_cache_key/options/retention.
stop accepts up to 4 sequences.
response_format.json_schema always runs in strict mode.
Message schema includes a developer role; the leading system or developer message is applied as the system prompt.
Function tools require a description.
stream_options.include_usage: usage arrives in a final chunk (empty choices) before data: [DONE]; usage only present when requested.
Usage carries prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens.
reasoning_effort accepts none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max; when omitted the provider default for that model applies and defaults vary by model.
Assistant messages and streamed deltas can carry reasoning_content (not a 'reasoning' field); replaying it in an assistant message preserves reasoning context across requests.

Errors use the OpenAI envelope {error:{code,message,param,type}}; type is invalid_request_error (4xx), rate_limit_error (429, rate limited or model overloaded) or server_error (5xx); Retry-After accompanies 429.

Orchestrator rate limiting: a 429 (rate limited or model overloaded) carries a Retry-After header; x-ratelimit-* headers are documented only for the Agent API (success responses: x-ratelimit-limit/remaining/used/reset; its 429s carry Retry-After and no x-ratelimit-*), not for the Orchestrator.
Response echoes the requested model id; billing always uses that model's published rates regardless of how the request was served.

Responses endpoint (/router/v1/responses) is stateless: store:true, background:true, non-null previous_response_id, max_tool_calls, top_logprobs, truncation:auto, file/video input, item references, text.format json_object and text.format.strict:false are rejected with 400.

The Agent API (base https://api.perplexity.ai/v1, POST /v1/agent aliased as /v1/responses) is Responses-style only and is a different product from the Orchestrator.
Agent API: for GPT-5, o1 and o3 families (e.g. openai/gpt-5.6-sol) temperature and top_p are silently ignored.

deviations.text: Model IDs are namespaced <provider>/<model_name>; OpenAI model strings such as gpt-4o or text-embedding-3-large return a 404.
Assistants, Threads and Runs are not implemented.
OpenAI-shaped fine_tuning.jobs, batches and moderations are not supported; files is only partial (Together has its own Files and Batch APIs).
logprobs returns Together's own shape, richer than OpenAI's.
seed is best-effort; determinism is not guaranteed across replicas, model versions or load.
n is supported on most chat models but not every model; loop client-side if a model rejects it.
logit_bias is not supported on most models.
service_tier, store, metadata and prediction are accepted but ignored.
reasoning_effort works on GPT-OSS models (low, medium, high); Together's reasoning={"enabled": ...} toggle and chat_template_kwargs are not part of OpenAI's API.
Vision models accept image_url with remote URLs and base64 data URIs; the detail field is accepted but ignored.

usage always has prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens; cached and reasoning token counts vary in location by model: reasoning models nest them OpenAI-style (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), some non-reasoning models return cached_tokens flat at the top level of usage. A client reading only one shape gets 0 with no error.
Reasoning models return the chain of thought in a 'reasoning' or 'reasoning_content' field on the assistant message (field name depends on the model), not OpenAI's nested reasoning object.
For multi-turn tool calling or preserved thinking, the reasoning must be passed back under the same key (reasoning or reasoning_content) on the prior assistant turn.
id and system_fingerprint are present but use Together's formats and should not be parsed as OpenAI ids.
Errors are OpenAI-shaped {"error": {"message", "type", "code"}} but type and code values are Together's; match on HTTP status (400, 401, 404, 429, 500, 503).
GPT-OSS reasoning guidance says to use the developer role message for system instructions.
Serverless rate limiting returns 429 or 503 under high demand; the rate-limits page documents no rate-limit response headers.

providers.notes: Read via curl through the agent proxy (WebFetch DNS fails). deviations.text: Chat Completions is documented as a legacy endpoint; new features arrive on the Responses API first (primary examples use /v1/responses).
presence_penalty, frequency_penalty and stop cannot be used with reasoning models; requests that include them return an error.
reasoning_effort is supported on grok-4.7, 4.6 and 4.5 (default high); reasoning cannot be disabled on those models, while grok-4.3 accepts none (default low).
reasoning_effort xhigh is available on grok-4.6 and later; on models that do not support it (grok-4.5) it is treated as high.

Reasoning is exposed through usage reasoning_tokens; on the Responses API grok-4.7 always returns reasoning.encrypted_content and a reasoning summary; no plaintext reasoning_content field is documented on Chat Completions.
Encrypted reasoning items must be passed back unchanged in the next request's input to keep reasoning across turns (Responses API).
logprobs and top_logprobs are not supported by grok-4.20 and newer models and are silently ignored if set.
No role order limitation: system, user and assistant roles can be mixed in any sequence.
Message content may be a list of {type:text} parts for system, user and assistant roles; image input uses image_url parts (jpg/jpeg or png, max 20MiB, no image-count limit, any text/image order).
The xAI API is stateless: prior turns must be resent with each Chat Completions request.

response_format json_schema (plus json_object and text) is supported; tool-call arguments always conform to the tool schema (strict implicitly true). Subset of JSON Schema: oneOf behaves as anyOf, allOf single subschema only, $ref non-circular only, additionalProperties defaults to false, minLength/maxLength guaranteed up to 2,048, minItems/maxItems 256, minProperties/maxProperties 64.

Structured schemas returning 400: enum or anyOf with zero variants, boolean property schemas, maxContains/minContains, items as an array; regex pattern excludes backreferences, \p{..}, \b, lookaround, inline modifiers.
usage.prompt_tokens_details carries text_tokens, audio_tokens, image_tokens and cached_tokens; every response also carries usage.cost_in_usd_ticks.

Rate limits are per-model requests per second and tokens per minute by spend tier (grok-4.3 Tier 0: 37 RPS, 10M TPM); exceeding any returns 429; no rate-limit response headers are documented on the pages read.
Prompts above the 200k-token long-context threshold bill the long-context rate for the whole request.

Requests to retired slugs (grok-4-fast-*, grok-4-1-fast-*, grok-4-0709, grok-3, grok-code-fast-1) are redirected to grok-4.3 (low effort for reasoning slugs, none for non-reasoning slugs) or grok-build-0.1.

stop: 'Currently, only one stop word is supported' (array form ["stop_word1"]; schema also says maxItems 4)

providers.name: OpenRouter

auth.notes: Authorization: Bearer <OPENROUTER_API_KEY>. Optional attribution headers HTTP-Referer, X-OpenRouter-Title (X-Title also accepted), X-OpenRouter-Categories.

models.notes: chat and reasoning use one pinned :free slug because openrouter/free picks a different free model per request (seen in a live run); openrouter/free (Free Models Router) is documented and appears in GET /api/v1/models with $0 pricing, 200K context, supported_parameters including reasoning/tools/structured_outputs; it picks a random free model per request, so pin a :free slug for repeatable probes. nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free is in the live models list with $0 pricing and supported_parameters reasoning, tools, structured_outputs (checked 2026-10-20); the free roster churns frequently.

deviations.text: If the chosen model does not support a request parameter (e.g. logit_bias on non-OpenAI models, top_k for OpenAI), the parameter is ignored; the rest are forwarded to the underlying model API.

Streaming: on Chat Completions every stream ends with an extra usage chunk just before [DONE]; unlike OpenAI's spec it carries a non-empty choices array (one content-free delta repeating finish_reason and native_finish_reason), so finish_reason appears twice. Usage is returned without requesting stream_options. Usage also carries cost, cost_details, is_byok.

SSE streams occasionally contain comment lines (': OPENROUTER PROCESSING') that parsers must skip; an error after streaming starts arrives as an SSE data event with an error field and the HTTP status stays 200.

Reasoning is configured via a `reasoning` object (effort, summary, enabled/max_tokens/exclude) and the shorthand top-level reasoning_effort (max, xhigh, high, medium, low, minimal, none); they cannot differ if both are sent. Assistant messages carry `reasoning` (string) and `reasoning_details`, not reasoning_content.

max_tokens and max_completion_tokens share semantics; for reasoning models the limit covers reasoning plus visible output on most providers, so a small value can return 200 with finish_reason length and empty content.
Responses API (/api/v1/responses) is stateless: requests that set store: true or a non-null previous_response_id are rejected with a 400 error.

Error body is {error:{code:number,message,metadata?}} with HTTP status equal to error.code; documented codes 400, 401, 402, 403, 408, 429, 502, 503; Retry-After may accompany 429/503/402; the Responses API error body uses string codes (e.g. invalid_prompt) and a top-level metadata field.

Successful inference responses do not include X-RateLimit-* headers; only OpenRouter-originated platform-limit errors carry X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset (and Retry-After when every attempted provider returned a hint); remaining quota via GET /api/v1/key.

OpenRouter selects the least expensive/best provider for the model and falls back to other providers on 5xx or rate limits; responses are normalized to the OpenAI Chat schema and carry extra fields (native_finish_reason, cost, reasoning_details, models/route/provider/plugins request fields).
If message `name` is included it is prepended as '{name}: {content}' for non-OpenAI models; content parts are only for the user role; image_url accepts a URL or base64 data with optional detail.
Message schema includes system, user, assistant, tool and developer roles; a trailing assistant message is treated as a prefill.
response_format json_object and json_schema are supported but depend on the routed model (check models page supported_parameters=structured_outputs).
tool_choice none/auto/required/function is documented; tools are mapped or templated for non-OpenAI providers, so support is per model.
stop accepts up to 4 sequences (schema maxItems 4); temperature range [0,2].
Free model limits (ids ending :free): 20 requests/min and 50/day with less than $10 credits purchased all-time; 20/min and 1000/day with at least $10.

providers.notes: Official overview, parameters, streaming, errors, limits, Responses and chat-completion OpenAPI pages all read. models.notes: Model naming: plain Snowflake catalog names with a family prefix, e.g. openai-gpt-5, openai-gpt-5-nano, claude-sonnet-4-5, llama3.1-8b, mistral-large2, deepseek-r1, snowflake-llama-3.3-70b; fine-tuned models use database.schema.model. anthropic_messages_endpoint.source: official-page (Cortex REST API page: Messages API, Claude models only; Anthropic SDK base_url is .../api/v2/cortex and needs the Authorization Bearer header overridden)

deviations.text: max_tokens is deprecated and returns an error for OpenAI, Claude and other model families; use max_completion_tokens
max_completion_tokens supported for all families; defaults to 4096 when unset; theoretical maximum 131,072; each model has its own output limit (rate-limit table lists 16,384)
messages[].role: OpenAI models supported; Claude and other models only user, assistant, system (developer role not supported for them)
messages[].name supported for OpenAI models, ignored for Claude and other models

Image content parts: image_url supported for OpenAI and Claude models, error for other models; images must be base64-encoded, max 20 per conversation, 20 MiB max request size; image input for claude-sonnet-4-5 and newer, openai-gpt-4.1 and newer

Content parts type text supported for all; file content part errors for OpenAI and Claude (ignored for other); input_audio errors for OpenAI (ignored for others); audio and messages[].audio error for OpenAI models, ignored for others; audio not supported
tools: supported for OpenAI models, only function tools for Claude models, error for other models; tool calling supported for OpenAI and Claude models only
tool_choice supported for OpenAI models, only function tools for Claude, ignored for other models; parallel_tool_calls supported for OpenAI only (ignored otherwise)
response_format: supported for OpenAI models; Claude models only json_schema; ignored for other models; json_schema is the documented structured-output form
stream_options.include_usage supported for all families; stream_options.include_obfuscation ignored; default usage behavior not documented

usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens: OpenAI models report cache reads only, Claude reads and writes, other models not supported. Prompt caching: OpenAI implicit for prompts of 1,024+ tokens; Claude explicit via cache_control (ephemeral only, 5-minute TTL, max 4 breakpoints); cache_control and prompt_cache_key ignored for non-supporting families

reasoning_effort: supported for OpenAI models (values none, minimal, low, medium, high), ignored for Claude and other models; reasoning.effort overrides reasoning_effort for OpenAI, is converted to reasoning.max_tokens for Claude, ignored for other; reasoning.max_tokens ignored for OpenAI, supported for Claude

temperature is ignored for Claude Opus 4.7 (model no longer supports it); temperature and top_p supported for all families
n supported for OpenAI models, ignored for Claude and other models (choices[].index single choice only for those)
logprobs and top_logprobs supported for OpenAI models, ignored for Claude and other models; choices[].logprobs not supported in their responses
stop supported for OpenAI models, ignored for Claude and other models
frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, logit_bias, prediction, verbosity supported for OpenAI models only (ignored for others); prompt_cache_key OpenAI only
service_tier and store return errors for all model families; metadata, modalities, safety_identifier ignored for all families; web_search_options errors for OpenAI models, ignored for others

Response fields: choices[].finish_reason not supported for Claude, only 'stop' for other models; delta.role, refusal, function_call not supported for Claude/other; system_fingerprint and service_tier in the response only for OpenAI models

Response headers openai-organization, openai-version, openai-processing-ms, x-ratelimit-limit/remaining/reset-requests and -tokens, and retry-after are all documented as not supported; rate limits are per account and per model, 429 'too many requests' on exceeding RPM/TPM

Errors: statuses are 400 (invalid options object, unknown model, schema validation failed, max tokens exceeded, all requests throttled by remote service), 402 budget exceeded, 403 not authorized, 429 too many requests, 503 inference timed out; error messages are generated by Snowflake, not by the model provider.
